note: A retirement is a preservation claim, not a story about a red run. Every entry registers the retired path (file), the original path it was retired from (original_path), the sha256 of the preserved bytes (the retirement's retired_sha256), the commit the file was retired from (retired_from_commit), a free-text reason, the registration date (retired_on) and the review that accepted the retirement (review_reference). scripts/verify-retirement-registry.js reads no test output. It checks: (a) preserved - the file at the registered path hashes to the registered sha256, so the registered bytes cannot be deleted or edited; (b) complete - every file under tests/legacy/ is registered; (c) not a fake retirement - the original path does not still carry the registered bytes; (d) re-evaluable - the registered bytes are put back at the original path and run, and a passing run is named as a receipt (KDNA-RETIREMENT-RESTORABLE); an entry whose bytes cannot be run there records reeval_in_place not-possible with a reeval_note instead (tests/legacy/pd275/terminal.test.js is such an entry: the helper it requires is retired material too); (e) re-checkable - the gate computes C_last, the newest commit on HEAD whose tree still carries the file at original_path, refuses any entry that names a different commit (so a retirement cannot be anchored at an older retirement that a later one superseded) and requires the named commit to be reachable from HEAD. Only (a)-(c) and (e) decide the exit code. What a machine cannot prove is that nobody wrote the file before the move, so the gate prints it instead of judging it: KDNA-RETIREMENT-DIFF (the first retirement changed the content while moving the file, full diff), KDNA-RETIREMENT-PRIOR-WRITE (the named commit wrote the file at the original path itself, full diff), and KDNA-RETIREMENT-WINDOW (later commits in the retirement window that modified or removed the retired copy, counted as content_changed_in_window, the retirement's own rewrite included). A non-zero window or a prior write needs an independent reviewer's per-entry signature - review_signature 'no-content-change', or 'change-explained' with a review_note holding the reason - before the entry may enter a push batch; entries that still lack one are printed as KDNA-RETIREMENT-UNSIGNED. Shape five - rewrite one byte, then move the file - is rc=0 with the change exposed and unsigned, never a red gate. The copies registered here are the pre-retirement files themselves; the first move changed content once (relative requires, __dirname paths and the path to bin/kdna-studio.js were re-pointed), its diff and the window are printed and counted, and the copies were restored to the bytes their original paths carried. The suites are red against the committed graph because the objects they exercise are gone from it; that is an independent observation, not a verdict.
